Foxtel to re-brand sports channels as Kayo Sports

By
Weekender Newsroom
-
September 3, 2026, 18:59

The Fox Sports brand is about to be no more.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:35
Instaread

DAZN has announced it will unify the Fox Sports and Kayo Sports brands next year, with its sports offering to be known as Kayo Sports.

It will end three decades of the Fox Sports brand in Australia.

DAZN recently secured a new long-term broadcast deal with the NRL and also has long-term arrangements with the AFL, motor sports and golf – along with other sports.

It was widely expected the brands would align at some stage with Foxtel, Binge and Kayo all currently operating as different brands but having crossover content.

Kayo has traditionally been a streaming-only brand but the traditional Fox Sports channels via set top boxes and satellites will now be known as Kayo.

The Weekender has confirmed the traditional service will still be known as Foxtel, with the channels being re-branded.

“With the global scale, capability and expertise of DAZN behind us, 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for Foxtel Group,” said Foxtel Group CEO Patrick Delany.

“An unrivalled sporting line-up with all tier-1 Australian sports locked in through to the next decade and beyond – all on Kayo SPORTS.

“A blockbuster entertainment slate packed with Australian Originals, international thrillers and a deep library of content from our over 100 studio and distribution partners – all on BINGE.

“And DAZN Media+ introducing more innovation and partnerships to ensure we connect brands with the stories and conversations that bring Australians together.”

While Foxtel has moved to a streaming focus, it has confirmed it remains committed to its traditional satellite service.
